newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel games delayed after fatal bridge collapse.
newsitem.headline: Israel games delayed after fatal bridge collapse.

text.p: An international Jewish sporting event has been postponed for a day of mourning after a bridge at an Israeli sports stadium collapsed at the event's opening ceremonies, killing one and injuring 64.

Scores of competitors from the 370-member Australian team were standing on a temporary bridge over the Yarkon River ready to lead a march into the Ramat Gan Stadium near Tel Aviv for the 27-nation Maccabiah Games nicknamed the "Jewish Olympics".
Police said one person was killed and 64 were injured, at least three seriously, when the wooden bridge supported by metal bars collapsed in the middle.
Israel's Itim news agency said the dead person was an Australian woman of about 50 years old but this could not be confirmed.
Tel Aviv district police chief Shlomo Aronishki said police had launched an investigation.
"I assume during the investigation...we will have to also question the people who built it," Aronishki told Israel radio.
Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told Reuters said there was no suspicion of foul play and an engineer had previously declared the bridge fit for use.
Israel Television broadcast pictures of a cluster of youngsters in muddied white sports uniforms amid the rubble of the bridge where it collapsed into the water.

"We were walking across. All of a sudden we heard a bang," Harry Purcell, the Australia team manager, told reporters. "And then all of a sudden in slow motion it just collapsed in the middle and we started to slide."

Organisers cancelled the march of national teams but a public storm erupted among organisers and politicians over the decision to proceed with entertainment for the 50,000 spectators present for the start of the quadrennial games.
A wet, shoeless and shirtless Australian named Zorek, a 15-year-old tennis player, described what he said was the worst experience of his life.
"I was under the water. I thought I was going to die. My head was under the water. I couldn't breathe for a minute until I felt the ground."
Some 40 minutes after the collapse, while rescuers formed human chains and marched into the marshy waters, Israeli President Ezer Weizman declared the games open.
"I am sorry this is the way to open the Maccabiah which should be more joyous and I hope that in this Maccabiah that there will be accomplishments that will make all of us happy," he told the crowd.
